Messages.Body:
Exactly when is the last opportunity to play SR in the HT example?
Can I wait until my vampire has been chosen? 'till the second before the
blood actually changes hands? Similarly, how about the Mprank? or the Mgame?

Also, what about Elder Intervention (cardname?) can I play it to cancel an
action after they have put some mods on it? Are they counted as having
attempted it for the NRA?

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
In article <6iopvb$n...@chile.earthlink.net>#1/1,

"PC Handyman" <pchan...@earthlink.net> wrote:
>
> Exactly when is the last opportunity to play SR in the HT example?

The last opportunity to play Sudden Reversal (SR) in any example is right
after the Master Card in question is played.

Note that all terms/targets/etc. of a master card are selected/announced
when the card is played, so that must happen before anything else,
including SR.

> Can I wait until my vampire has been chosen? 'till the second before the
> blood actually changes hands? Similarly, how about the Mprank? or the Mgame?

For Hostile Takeover, you can (indeed, must) wait until your vampire is
chosen, since choosing a vampire is part of playing the card.

At that point, before any bidding starts, you can play SR. This is
your only opportunity to play SR.

For Malkavian Prank, since there are no terms to be selected when the
card is played, you play SR immediately when the Mprank is played. You
cannot wait until after the player starts guessing the amounts of pool.

Likewise for Game of Malkav.

> Also, what about Elder Intervention (cardname?) can I play it to cancel an
> action after they have put some mods on it? Are they counted as having
> attempted it for the NRA?

Direct Intervention. Is also played immediately after the card you want to
cancel, or not at all.

This screws up some timing involving modifiers that must be played "as the
action is announced", so I'd suggest allowing the acting player to "undo"
such action modifiers (pick it back up, return the card drawn to replace
it back on the library, etc.). The clean solution to this is to announce
each action (and play the card) and then ask "any direct intervention?" before
going on to play the required action modifiers. But that's a bit cumbersome.
